prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Plan comparison (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Feature" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 83px
  col 2: header "Free" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 79px
  col 3: header "Pro" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 4: header "Enterprise" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 229px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 419px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A feature-by-feature plan comparison: readers check what each tier includes and use Notes for caveats.","reading":"Scan down the Feature column, then move horizontally across Free, Pro and Enterprise to compare the same capability; Notes is consulted only when a value needs explanation.","groups":["Free, Pro and Enterprise are parallel plan-value columns and should read as a comparable set","Feature is the row-label column that anchors each comparison","Notes is a secondary annotation column, not a fourth plan"],"keep_intact":["the headers Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes","short values such as 3, 2 GB, 100 GB, 30 days, 1 year, Custom and Email","Community and Unlimited where the chosen width permits","SSO / SAML as a single label"],"may_wrap":["Notes prose","24/7 phone & dedicated at its spaces","SSO / SAML at the slash if the Feature column is tight","long plan values at word boundaries when space is squeezed"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [82, 78, 64, 80, 55] · table 360×1404px · row heights [60, 292, 339, 362, 60, 292] · column headers wrapped 2/5 · tallest cell 15 lines · mid-word splits 26
Design r0B: widths [90, 100, 90, 110, 180] · table 571×405px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 83, 36, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 211px
Design r0C: widths [84, 92, 82, 102, 240] · table 601×358px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 2 · OVERFLOWS the box by 241px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
